scholarships.title: Chevening Scholarships for Master's Study in the United Kingdom
scholarships.summary: The UK government's fully funded one-year Master's award for emerging leaders from Chevening-eligible countries, covering tuition, a living stipend, travel and allowances.
scholarships.applicants: Professionals with 2+ years of work experience, any nationality eligible for Chevening
benefits: Full tuition fees paid directly to your chosen university
Monthly living stipend of £1,333 (London: £1,516)
One return economy airfare to the UK
Arrival and departure allowances
Thesis and study grants
requirements: Return to your country of citizenship for at least two years after the scholarship ends
Hold a relevant undergraduate degree equivalent to an upper second-class UK honours degree
Have at least two years (2,880 hours) of work experience, whether paid or voluntary
Apply to and receive an unconditional offer for up to three eligible UK courses
Meet the English language requirement (IELTS 6.5 overall, 5.5 in each component) before the deadline
documents: IELTS / TOEFL / PTE English test result
Up to four UK university course offers via UFES
Curriculum vitae describing your leadership and networking record
howToApply: Create an account on the Chevening online application system (UFES) before the closing date.
Complete all four essay questions on leadership, networking, career plan and study in the UK.
Add your three preferred UK Master's courses and both references.
Submit and upload supporting documents — incomplete applications are not considered.
Shortlisted candidates attend an interview at the British High Commission between February and April.
Final results are released in June, with the programme beginning in September.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

scholarships.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program — University of British Columbia
scholarships.summary: A fully funded graduate award for African students admitted to selected Master's programs at UBC, paired with mentorship, a transition-to-work program and a global alumni network.
scholarships.provider: Mastercard Foundation & University of British Columbia
scholarships.applicants: Graduates from African countries with a demonstrated record of community leadership
benefits: Full tuition and student fees for the length of the program
Living allowance and settlement support
One-way airfare to Vancouver
Laptop, study materials and health coverage allowance
Paid internship placement and career coaching after graduation
requirements: Citizen of and ordinarily resident in an African country
Hold a four-year undergraduate degree (or equivalent) with a B+ average (76%)
Be admitted to one of the eligible UBC Master's programs before the funding deadline
Demonstrate leadership in your community through work, volunteering or enterprise
Not have previously completed a graduate degree
documents: Statement of leadership and community impact (max 1,500 words)
Official transcripts in certified English translation
Admission offer letter from UBC (may follow before final selection)
howToApply: Apply for admission to an eligible UBC graduate program through the UBC online application.
In the funding section of the application, select the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program.
Submit the additional leadership statement and supporting documents before the program deadline.
Shortlisted scholars are interviewed online in November and December.
Results are issued with admission offers in January, for a September intake.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

scholarships.title: Swiss Government Excellence Research Scholarships for PhD Candidates
scholarships.summary: Postgraduate research scholarships for doctoral and postdoctoral students to pursue a PhD or research fellowship at a Swiss cantonal university, ETH domain or federal institute.
scholarships.provider: Swiss Confederation — Federal Commission for Scholarships
scholarships.applicants: Master's graduates and early-career researchers with an accepted PhD research proposal
benefits: CHF 1,920 per month living stipend for the full grant period
Tuition fee exemption at the host institution
Half-fare travel card across Switzerland
Health insurance covered for the grant duration
Mandatory research supervision by a Swiss professor
requirements: Hold a master's degree awarded no more than three years before the application deadline
Not hold Swiss nationality and not have previously been funded by the Swiss government
Contact and secure informal agreement from a professor willing to supervise your research
No more than one previous postdoctoral fellowship of up to one year
Complete application submitted through the Federal Commission's online form
documents: Research proposal of up to five pages signed by the supervising professor
Master's degree certificate and full transcripts
Signed supervision letter from the host professor
howToApply: Identify a Swiss supervising professor whose research matches your proposal.
Download and complete the application form from the FCS portal.
Compile all documents and upload them before the October deadline.
Application documents are reviewed by the Federal Commission between November and March.
Results are announced in May, with the grant starting the following September.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

scholarships.title: MTN Foundation Science & Technology Undergraduate Scholarship Scheme
scholarships.summary: An annual Nigerian undergraduate scholarship for full-time students in accredited universities, awarding tuition support across the sciences, engineering and information technology.
scholarships.applicants: Full-time Nigerian undergraduates in year 2–5 of an accredited university program
benefits: Tuition support paid directly to your institution for the academic session
Book and research allowance
Annual renewal subject to a minimum CGPA of 3.5
Access to MTN internship and graduate recruitment pipelines
requirements: Nigerian citizen currently enrolled full-time in an accredited university
Studying science, engineering, ICT, agriculture or a closely related discipline
Completed year 2 with a minimum CGPA of 3.5/5.0 or its equivalent
Not in receipt of any other scholarship for the same academic session
Available for the online computer-based test and a verification interview
documents: Current academic transcript signed by the registrar
Proof of admission or student identity card
NIN and bank account details in the applicant's name
howToApply: Complete the online application form on the MTN Foundation scholarship portal before the deadline.
Upload your transcript, admission letter and passport photograph.
Sit the scheduled computer-based aptitude test at an accredited centre.
Shortlisted candidates attend a verification interview with their original documents.
Successful scholars are notified and payments are released to their institution.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

scholarships.title: Commonwealth Shared Scholarships for Master's Study in the UK
scholarships.summary: UK-funded scholarships for students from developing Commonwealth countries who would not otherwise be able to study in the UK, offered across a list of partner university courses.
scholarships.provider: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK
scholarships.applicants: Citizens of an eligible developing Commonwealth country with a relevant undergraduate degree
benefits: Full tuition fees at the host UK university
Living allowance of £1,347 per month (£1,668 in London)
Return airfare to your home country
Thesis and research grant
Warm clothing allowance where applicable
requirements: Be a citizen of, or be granted refugee status in, an eligible developing Commonwealth country
Be permanently resident in a developing Commonwealth country
Hold a first degree of at least upper second-class honours standard
Not have undertaken studies for one academic year or more in a developed country
Be confirmed for admission on one of the listed UKMSSA partner courses
Not have applied for the same course in a previous cycle
documents: Two references, at least one academic
Evidence of your chosen UKMSSA course offer
howToApply: Check the list of eligible UKMSSA courses published with this year's offer.
Apply for admission to your chosen course directly through the UK university.
Apply for the scholarship through the CSC online application system.
Submit both applications before the January deadline — the scholarship alone is not enough.
Nominations are confirmed by the UK university between March and May.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

scholarships.title: Aga Khan Foundation International Scholarship Programme
scholarships.summary: A competitive, need-based award for students from developing countries pursuing postgraduate study, awarded as a 50% grant and 50% loan, with repayment beginning after studies end.
scholarships.applicants: Students under 30 from developing countries admitted to a recognised postgraduate institution
benefits: 50% grant and 50% loan of tuition and living costs
Loan repayments begin one year after studies are completed
Academic and career mentoring through the Foundation's network
Recognition through the Foundation's global alumni community
requirements: Citizen of a developing country where AKF is active
Under 30 years of age at the time of application
Admitted to a high-quality postgraduate program at a reputable institution
Demonstrated financial need with no other substantial funding in place
Strong academic record and a clear plan to return and contribute to your country
documents: Financial statement and family income evidence
Completed AKF application form submitted through the national agency
howToApply: Download the application form from the Aga Khan Foundation national office in your country.
Complete the form with your admission letter and financial evidence.
Submit the application to the designated national agency before the March deadline.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed by a local selection committee.
Final results are communicated in June.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

scholarships.title: DAAD Helmut Schmidt Programme — Public Policy and Good Governance (Master's)
scholarships.summary: Germany's flagship scholarship for future leaders from transition and developing countries, offering English-taught Master's degrees in public policy, governance and development.
scholarships.applicants: Graduates in political science, law, economics, public administration or a related field
benefits: Tuition-free enrolment at eight partner German universities
Monthly stipend of €992
Health, accident and liability insurance cover
Travel allowance and German language course
Research and thesis funding in the second year
requirements: First degree completed within the last six years
At least two years of professional experience in the public sector, NGO or media
English proficiency at C1 level (IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 90) or German C1 for German-taught tracks
Strong academic record and a letter of recommendation from your employer or university
Willingness to return to your home country after the programme
documents: Two letters of recommendation, one academic and one professional
Employer's release and confirmation of professional experience
howToApply: Choose up to two of the eight partner universities listed in the programme brochure.
Register in the DAAD portal and complete the online application form.
Upload all supporting documents in the portal before the August deadline.
A pre-selection committee reviews applications in October and November.
Selected candidates are interviewed in December and notified in January.
scholarships.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

schoolUpdates.title: Post-UTME screening registration opens for 2025/2026 admission seekers
schoolUpdates.summary: UNILAG has opened its online Post-UTME screening portal for candidates who chose the university as first choice and scored at least 200 in the 2025 UTME.
schoolUpdates.appliesTo: All 2025 UTME candidates who scored 200 or above and listed UNILAG as first choice, including direct-entry applicants holding OND, HND or NCE results.
requirements: 2025 UTME result slip showing a score of 200 or above
O'level results with at least five credits including English Language and Mathematics
Confirmation that UNILAG is your first choice institution on JAMB CAPS
Payment reference for the ₦2,000 screening fee
Recent passport photograph in JPEG format, not larger than 50KB
steps: Visit the UNILAG Post-UTME portal and create an account with your JAMB registration number.
Pay the screening fee online using a card, transfer or bank branch payment.
Complete the bio-data form and upload your O'level result and passport photograph.
Print the completed application slip and bring it to your assigned screening centre.
Monitor JAMB CAPS for your admission status — confirmation on CAPS is the only valid admission.
schoolUpdates.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

schoolUpdates.title: Correction of data window: fix names, date of birth and institution choices
schoolUpdates.summary: JAMB has reopened its correction of data service, allowing candidates to fix mismatches in names, date of birth and first-choice institution before admission processing begins.
schoolUpdates.appliesTo: Candidates whose JAMB profiles contain an incorrect name, date of birth, state of origin or first-choice institution — especially those awaiting O'level uploads.
requirements: Original JAMB registration slip
Valid government-issued ID showing your correct name and date of birth
O'level scratch card or result checker details for re-upload
₦1,500 service charge per correction, payable only at an accredited centre
steps: Visit the nearest accredited JAMB CBT centre with your registration slip and ID.
Request the specific correction — name, date of birth, state of origin or institution.
Pay the service fee at the centre and confirm the change on the printed acknowledgement slip.
For O'level results, confirm the upload and check that all five credits appear under your JAMB profile.
Re-check your JAMB CAPS the following week to confirm the correction took effect.
schoolUpdates.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

schoolUpdates.title: 2026 Batch 'C' Stream I mobilisation timetable released
schoolUpdates.summary: The NYSC has published the mobilisation timetable for Batch C Stream I, covering online registration, printing of call-up letters and the date of reporting to orientation camps.
schoolUpdates.appliesTo: Graduates of Nigerian and foreign institutions whose names have been submitted for mobilisation by their respective institutions.
requirements: Graduation certificate or statement of results
Valid NYSC registration account with a passport photograph
Call-up letter printed in colour
Original tenement/history of service letter for foreign-trained graduates
Medical fitness certificate from a government hospital where required
steps: Log in to the NYSC portal with your matriculation number and password.
Confirm that your institution has uploaded your details to the mobilisation list.
Complete bi-data verification and upload your passport photograph if not already done.
Print your call-up letter from the stated date and note your camp address and reporting date.
Report to the orientation camp on the scheduled date with your originals and photocopies.
schoolUpdates.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

schoolUpdates.title: School fees payment and course registration deadline extended by two weeks
schoolUpdates.summary: UNN has extended the deadline for payment of school fees and completion of course registration for the second semester, following requests from student representatives.
schoolUpdates.appliesTo: All returning undergraduates of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka who have not completed second-semester fee payment and online course registration.
requirements: Student matriculation number
Remita payment reference generated from the UNN student portal
Departmental course adviser approval for your registered courses
Evidence of payment of any outstanding departmental or faculty levy
steps: Log in to the UNN student portal and select the second-semester fee item.
Generate a Remita reference and pay at any bank branch or with a debit card.
Return to the portal and upload your payment confirmation slip.
Select your courses online and submit for your departmental adviser's approval.
Print the signed course registration form and keep it for examination clearance.
schoolUpdates.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

schoolUpdates.title: First batch admission list published — confirm your offer on JAMB CAPS
schoolUpdates.summary: ABU has released its first batch list of admitted candidates. Applicants are required to accept their offers on JAMB CAPS to be considered fully admitted.
schoolUpdates.appliesTo: Candidates who chose Ahmadu Bello University as first choice and scored at least 180 in the 2025 UTME and have the required O'level credits.
requirements: 2025 UTME result slip with the minimum departmental cut-off
O'level result with the required subject combination
Original JAMB admission letter after accepting on CAPS
Evidence of acceptance fee payment
Local government identification certificate
steps: Log in to jamb.gov.ng/efacility and open your JAMB CAPS profile.
Select 'Check Admission Status' and then 'Accept Admission' if an offer is displayed.
Print your JAMB admission letter — this is required for all screening and registration.
Pay the acceptance fee through the ABU portal and print the payment confirmation.
Attend the physical screening at your faculty with all original documents.
schoolUpdates.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

jobs.title: Data Analyst Intern (Graduate Intake)
jobs.summary: A six-month paid internship for detail-first graduates, supporting payments analytics across Nigeria and West Africa markets.
jobs.description: The payments analytics team turns raw transaction data into decisions for product, risk and commercial teams. This internship suits a graduate who is comfortable with spreadsheets and SQL and wants to learn production analytics inside a fast-moving payments company.
responsibilities: Build and maintain weekly dashboards for payment volume, success rates and merchant performance.
Run ad-hoc analysis on transaction data and explain findings in plain language.
Validate data quality across internal pipelines and flag anomalies to the data engineering team.
Support pricing, risk and growth teams with recurring reporting.
Document metrics definitions so the team uses one consistent version of each number.
requirements: Degree in statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science or a related quantitative field.
Solid SQL: joins, window functions and aggregations.
Comfortable in Excel or Google Sheets, including lookups and pivot tables.
Exposure to Python or R for analysis (pandas, matplotlib) is an advantage.
Clear written communication and an ability to work three days a week from our Yaba office.
jobs.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

jobs.title: Audit Graduate Trainee Programme 2026
jobs.summary: A structured two-year audit traineeship for young graduates, combining professional certification support with real client engagements from the first month.
jobs.description: The Audit Graduate Trainee Programme is KPMG Nigeria's entry route into the audit and assurance practice. Trainees rotate across financial services, energy and consumer markets engagements while working towards a professional qualification with full firm sponsorship.
responsibilities: Plan and execute audit testing under the supervision of an engagement manager.
Prepare working papers and reconcile client schedules to the general ledger.
Support year-end reporting and the preparation of financial statements.
Assess internal control procedures and document findings.
Build strong client relationships during on-site fieldwork.
requirements: Minimum of a second-class upper degree in accounting, finance, economics or a related discipline.
NYSC discharge certificate or exemption (for Nigerian applicants).
Maximum of two years of post-graduation experience.
Strong analytical skills and a willingness to begin ACCA or ICAN professional papers.
Available for the online assessment and panel interview in November.
jobs.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

jobs.title: Young Professionals Programme (YPP) — 2027 Cohort
jobs.summary: The Bank's flagship two-year entry programme for young African professionals, offering rotations across private sector, infrastructure, agriculture and human capital departments.
jobs.description: The Young Professionals Programme recruits and develops the next generation of African Development Bank staff. Selected candidates complete a structured two-year journey with departmental rotations, a leadership curriculum and a final placement in a core vice-presidency.
responsibilities: Support the preparation of country strategies, sector studies and project appraisals.
Contribute to the design and supervision of sovereign and non-sovereign operations.
Prepare board documents, policy briefs and portfolio performance reports.
Engage with governments, implementing agencies and development partners.
Complete assigned rotations and leadership development modules on schedule.
requirements: Citizen of an African Development Bank member country, aged 32 or below at application.
Master's degree in economics, finance, engineering, public policy, agriculture or a related field.
Minimum of three years of relevant professional or research experience.
Fluency in English and/or French; knowledge of the other is a strong advantage.
Commitment to a two-year residency in Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.
jobs.salary: Stated by the Bank: USD 75,400 – 96,800 base pay, plus allowances and benefits
jobs.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

jobs.title: Customer Experience Graduate Trainee
jobs.summary: A 12-month graduate trainee programme in Safaricom's customer experience function, rotating through digital channels, retail service and contact centre operations.
jobs.description: Customer Experience at Safaricom looks after millions of subscribers across voice, digital and retail touchpoints. Graduate trainees spend twelve months rotating through service design, contact centre operations, digital self-service and retail experience before taking up a permanent specialist role.
responsibilities: Analyse customer journey data and identify points of friction.
Support the rollout of self-service and chatbot flows.
Prepare weekly service performance reporting for leadership.
Shadow frontline teams in retail and contact centre environments.
Conduct customer research and present findings to the experience board.
requirements: Bachelor's degree completed between 2024 and 2026 in any discipline.
Kenyan citizen or permanent resident with the right to work in Kenya.
Demonstrated interest in customer experience, analytics or digital product work.
Strong presentation skills and comfort working with data.
Willingness to be based in Nairobi for the duration of the programme.
jobs.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

jobs.title: Associate Software Engineer — Remote, Africa
jobs.summary: An entry-level engineering role for graduates who have shipped projects through a bootcamp, self-study or a degree and want to work with global clients from day one.
jobs.description: Andela connects African engineers with global product teams. This associate role is designed for developers with a solid foundation and evidence of shipped work who are ready to contribute to a client codebase under mentorship.
responsibilities: Write, review and test code as part of an agile delivery team.
Participate in stand-ups, code reviews and retrospectives with a global client team.
Fix bugs and contribute small features under senior supervision.
Write documentation for the features you ship.
Complete weekly engineering practice sessions and technical assessments.
requirements: Portfolio of at least two projects on GitHub with clear README documentation.
Working knowledge of JavaScript, Python, Java or Go and one web framework.
Familiarity with Git, REST APIs and relational databases.
Reliable broadband connection and a quiet workspace.
Available for the technical screening and a live pairing session.
jobs.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

opportunities.title: Mandela Washington Fellowship for Young African Leaders
opportunities.summary: A six-week intensive leadership programme at a U.S. university for Africans aged 25–35, followed by a summit in Washington, D.C. and continuing alumni support.
eligibility: Citizen of a sub-Saharan African country, aged 25–35 at the time of application.
Currently residing in and working in a sub-Saharan African country.
Not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and not currently studying in the United States.
Proficient in English.
Not a current or former employee of the U.S. government or of the Mandela Washington Fellowship.
benefits: Six-week academic and leadership institute at a host U.S. university.
Round-trip airfare, accommodation, meals and programme costs fully covered.
Travel allowance and any applicable visa fees reimbursed.
Invitation to the Washington, D.C. Summit for the full cohort.
Ongoing alumni funding, mentorship and networking after the programme.
process: Complete the online application, including two short essays on leadership and community impact.
Provide two references who can speak to your professional work.
Submit before the October deadline — no late applications are accepted.
Semifinalists are interviewed by the U.S. Embassy or implementing partner between November and January.
Finalists are notified in March, with travel arranged for June.
opportunities.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

opportunities.title: Tony Elumelu Foundation Entrepreneurship Programme (TEEP)
opportunities.summary: A 12-week business programme for African entrepreneurs aged 18–39 offering seed funding of US$5,000, mentorship and access to the Foundation's investor network.
eligibility: African entrepreneur aged 18–39 at the time of application.
Business idea or early-stage venture based in any of the 54 African countries.
Business operates in one of the Foundation's focus sectors: agriculture, technology, manufacturing, retail, health or energy.
Founder is able to commit to the full 12-week online programme.
Venture has been operating for no more than three years.
benefits: US$5,000 non-refundable seed capital for successful applicants.
12 weeks of digital business training covering strategy, marketing and finance.
A dedicated mentor matched to your sector.
Access to the TEF alumni network of 12,000+ African founders.
Opportunity to pitch to investors at the annual showcase.
process: Create an account on the Tony Elumelu Foundation entrepreneurial portal.
Complete the business profile, market analysis and financial projections sections.
Upload your identity document and any existing registration certificate.
Applications are reviewed by the Foundation's selection panel over six weeks.
Selected founders begin training in January and receive funding after module four.
opportunities.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

opportunities.title: Hult Prize OnCampus Challenge — Build a Social Enterprise
opportunities.summary: A campus-level startup competition where student teams compete for a US$1,000,000 seed fund by solving a social problem outlined in this year's annual challenge question.
eligibility: Enrolled undergraduate or graduate students of any accredited university.
Teams of three to four members, at least half of whom must be from the same campus.
Open to all disciplines — no business or engineering degree required.
Each campus may register a limited number of teams, so apply early.
benefits: Campus champion award and a place in the regional accelerator.
Access to the US$1,000,000 global seed fund for the winning team.
Mentorship from Hult Prize staff, investors and founders.
A structured curriculum for launching a measurable social enterprise.
Global visibility and an invitation to the international summit.
process: Register your team and nominate a campus director or request an OnCampus programme.
Attend the challenge launch briefing to understand this year's question.
Submit a ten-slide concept deck describing the problem, solution and impact model.
Pitch at your campus finals; winners advance to the regional accelerator.
Regional winners receive funding support to build a working prototype.
opportunities.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

opportunities.title: ALX AI Career Essentials — Professional Certificate Cohort
opportunities.summary: A seven-week part-time programme preparing African young professionals to use generative AI tools productively in the workplace, closing with a verified certificate.
eligibility: Aged 18–34 and resident in an African country.
A laptop or desktop and reliable internet access for weekly live sessions.
No prior AI or programming experience required.
Commitment to approximately 10 hours per week for seven weeks.
benefits: Seven weeks of guided, project-based learning at no cost to admitted learners.
Live weekly sessions with mentors and a private peer community.
Portfolio projects demonstrating applied AI workflows.
Verified digital certificate on completion of all assessments.
Pathway into ALX's software engineering and data programmes.
process: Submit the short application form on the ALX admissions portal.
Complete a brief motivation questionnaire about your career goals.
Receive an admission email with your cohort start date within seven days.
Activate your learner account and attend the orientation session.
Complete weekly projects and the final assessment to earn your certificate.
opportunities.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

opportunities.title: One Young World Summit 2027 — Delegate Scholarships
opportunities.summary: Scholarship places for outstanding young leaders aged 18–30 to attend the One Young World Summit, covering registration, accommodation and travel for selected applicants.
eligibility: Aged 18–30 at the time of the Summit.
Demonstrated track record of leadership or impact in your community or field.
Available to attend the full duration of the Summit in person.
Fluent in English — the working language of the Summit.
Scholarship applicants must be referred by a One Young World Ambassador or an accredited organisation.
benefits: Full Summit registration and delegate access to all plenaries and workshops.
Accommodation and meals for the duration of the Summit.
Return travel for scholarship recipients from a limited number of regions.
Membership of the One Young World Ambassador network after the event.
Access to year-round community events and leadership programmes.
process: Create a profile on the One Young World application portal.
Complete the scholarship questions on your impact and leadership experience.
Add your referee's contact details — they will be asked to confirm your application.
Submit before the December deadline; shortlisted applicants are interviewed online.
Scholarship awards are announced in February 2027.
opportunities.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa

opportunities.title: AIESEC Global Community Development Exchange
opportunities.summary: A six-to-eight week volunteer and leadership exchange abroad, working with local organisations on education, sustainability and community development projects.
eligibility: Aged 18–30 and currently a student or recent graduate.
Passport valid for at least six months beyond the exchange end date.
Working proficiency in English; local language skills are an asset.
Able to self-fund the programme fee and travel, or secure a sponsoring employer.
Available for the full six-to-eight week duration.
benefits: Placement with a vetted local organisation in one of AIESEC's 120+ countries.
Pre-departure cultural and project preparation training.
Accommodation and meals arranged by the host committee in most placements.
Certificate of completion and documented international experience.
Lifelong access to the AIESEC alumni network.
process: Register on the AIESEC Opportunity Portal and complete your profile.
Filter opportunities by the Community Development category and your preferred continent.
Apply to a specific placement and complete the online interview with the receiving country.
Receive your acceptance letter and pay the programme fee.
Complete the pre-departure training before travelling to your host country.
opportunities.imageCredit: Official provider artwork · via Edusphere Africa
